clauses.reason: Executive Order 10951, signed 1961-06-29, is a one-sentence order under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947. It commands one thing: it extends the time within which the board of inquiry created by Executive Order 10949 must report to the President ("I hereby extend until" 9 a.m., July 3, 1961). That is a report deadline, recorded inclusively as running through 9 a.m. on 1961-07-03, with the exclusive reading (the extension ends when that moment begins) as the alternative; it is a deadline and a later event of EO 10949, and it is not an end (owner rulings 2026-10-21 until-dates and report deadline). The order has no termination clause of its own, and no held text gives the date on which the board actually reported, so the order was functionally spent no later than 1961-07-03 only if the board reported by then, which the held evidence does not establish. First end: Executive Order 12553, signed 1986-02-25, revokes this order by number. The cited source is the enacting sentence of EO 12553, which says "longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" The dossier records an agent-located acting provision for this pair that an independent AI review upheld (a hypothesis, not a certification). The table in EO 12553 (page 12 of the held Federal Register text, outside the cited enacting sentence) lists this order on its own row beginning at character offset 16252: the number 10951 followed by the subject Amending Executive Order No. 10949 creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting, which agrees with this order’s own title. EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording of its own (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become and similar words), so the date it was signed, 1986-02-25, is recorded as the end date. The held text also shows the filing date 1986-02-26 and the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03; those are the alternative readings and none of them changes the conclusion that the order was no longer in force after 1986-03-03.

research_rationale:
EO 10951 extends the report time of the EO 10949 board of inquiry; provisional status no. I read the held registered Federal Register text, confirmed identity from heading and number, and confirmed a single-clause inventory (the one-sentence extension). The extension deadline is a spent report deadline and not an end. EO 12553 (1986-02-25), which I read, revokes the order by number and is the first end shown in held evidence. The three machine searches carry no coverage warning and show no contrary hit.

savings.reason: EO 12553 has no saving, exception or pending-matters language: a search of the whole held text for except, notwithstanding, nothing in, saving, pending and similar words found only incidental uses inside other orders’ subject lines. The extension had no continuing effect after the board’s report time passed; whatever the board did, and any later proceedings under the Labor-Management Relations Act, rest on that Act and on EO 10949, not on this extension.
